adaptive_tick_binding, player_tick dispatch, adaptive mandatory barriers

reviewed_sources.fact: The retained video mode is 320x192x16 with a 30,720-byte framebuffer.

inputs.source_hash_scope: The four assembly-file hashes above match between the read-only main snapshot and the owned tmx-screen-prep worktree.

clock_totals.summary_scope_reconciliation: velocity-irq-summary.json reports max_debt=0 over its 74 retained commit-changed publication states. The raw trace has 128 IRQ snapshots and reaches AD_DEBT=1 on 21 non-retained snapshots. The values describe different sample sets.

confirmed_trace_facts.source_clock_rule: adaptive_batch computes elapsed=AD_BEGIN-AD_LAST, adds AD_DEBT, updates AD_LAST, and when AD_DUE is reached processes up to four one-tick callbacks. Each callback increments AD_SIM and subtracts one from AD_DEBT. Thus raw_frame-AD_LAST and AD_DEBT must be kept distinct; an IRQ snapshot can have stored debt zero while elapsed raw time has not yet been folded into that field.

effective_unfolded_plus_stored_clock_del.definition: raw_frame - adaptive.last_time + adaptive.debt, using the sample's current FRAMES value and source AD_LAST/AD_DEBT fields
effective_unfolded_plus_stored_clock_del.interpretation: This is the elapsed input the next eligible adaptive_batch will fold into AD_DEBT, not the stored AD_DEBT field.

confirmed_trace_facts.movement_units: The game uses 320x192 4bpp, so the row stride is 160 bytes. PLAYER_STEP is documented as a two-pixel step. Player/enemy horizontal pointer changes of one byte and vertical changes of 320 bytes both represent two screen pixels.

source_parity.player: adaptive_tick_binding copies the low byte of AD_SIM_TIME to LAST_FRAME and sets PLAYER_TICK_PENDING from its low parity bit. The normal callback calls player_tick only when pending is set. One player_tick moves one existing two-pixel step. Across the sampled Part-1 trace, player motion remains quantized in two-screen-pixel steps.
source_parity.roaming_enemy: enemy_tick_impl admits movement only when LAST_FRAME parity is even. Each admitted tick moves the active enemy one existing two-pixel step and advances its four-step pixel_phase.

player.same_phase_one_logical_tick_per_raw_base: With 23 logical ticks from the same start parity, ticks 907..929 contain 12 player movement opportunities = 24 pixels. The measured 25 logical ticks add one opportunity, matching 26 pixels. The remaining 1-pixel difference from the scalar 23-pixel comparison is caused by comparing two-pixel quantized steps to an odd 23-pixel bound. The phase-aware candidate limit 2*ceil(23/2)=24 pixels is exceeded by 2 pixels.
player.actual_player_pixels: BUG-080 sample signatures match this window at every endpoint/intermediate IRQ sample; its independently captured FRONT pixels match every opaque pixel of the selected native source template in all 128 samples. Opaque count varies by pose (120 or 122), so the raw helper count field is not a per-sample pixel count.

enemy0.front_displacement: 22 observed movement steps: 14 one-byte horizontal steps plus 8 320-byte vertical steps; each is two screen pixels, total 44 pixels.
enemy0.same_phase_one_logical_tick_per_raw_base: With 41 logical ticks from the same start parity, ticks 972..1012 contain 21 enemy movement opportunities = 42 pixels. The measured 43 logical ticks add one opportunity, matching 44 pixels. The remaining 1-pixel difference from the scalar 41-pixel comparison is the two-pixel movement quantum at an odd interval endpoint. The phase-aware candidate limit 2*ceil(41/2)=42 pixels is exceeded by 2 pixels.
enemy0.physical_pixel_limit: Enemy displacement is from the published FRONT ledger and is not independently pixel-template-matched.

cumulative_windows.shared_window_result: Each cumulative window has two more AD_SIM intervals than raw Vbord intervals. The extra parity-selected movement opportunity accounts arithmetically for the additional two pixels above the phase-aware one-step-per-two-Vbord candidate limit: player 26 versus 24 pixels in 23 intervals; enemy ledger 44 versus 42 pixels in 41 intervals. Player pixels are independently validated; enemy pixels are not. This explains the measured trace arithmetic, not the reported symptom in all builds or a generally safe repair.

bounded_candidate_contract_review.status: candidate only; not approved, implemented, or fitted
bounded_candidate_contract_review.candidate_interpretation: For regular player and roaming-enemy movement, permit at most one existing two-pixel movement step per two raw publication Vbords. Over N raw Vbord intervals, require displacement no greater than 2*ceil(N/2) pixels per actor, with interval endpoints and pending image treatment defined.
bounded_candidate_contract_review.provisional_fit_to_observation: The candidate 2*ceil(N/2) bound is violated by both cumulative windows by one existing two-pixel step: 26>24 for the player over 23 raw intervals, and 44>42 for the enemy FRONT ledger over 41. The player trace also has two pixel-validated 4-pixel changes; each occurs over two raw intervals from prior commit to new commit, and as a 4-pixel adjacent displayed-image change after one held image. In the first, the logical player is already four pixels ahead while FRONT is held. Source parity and the two extra AD_SIM intervals explain the measured arithmetic, but do not prove the reported symptom across builds or select a remedy.
bounded_candidate_contract_review.metric_gate: Count raw FRAMES/Vbord intervals and compare actor pixels at every IRQ return, including held FRONT images; use FB_COMMIT_SEQ only as secondary publication metadata. Define pending-image ownership, special-frame exemptions, actor-specific pixel displacement, and whether phase allowance is measured over raw time or only commit changes. A commit-only average can hide the observed held-image-to-burst transition.
insufficient_alternatives: A maximum of two AD_SIM ticks per adaptive_batch call alone is insufficient for the one-step-per-two-Vbord contract: at AD_RATE=1, one two-pixel actor step could still be published on each raw Vbord.

A minimum two-Vbord spacing between commits alone is insufficient: both observed four-pixel player changes already occur two raw intervals after the preceding commit, and the logical batch composed two movement steps into one image.
A per-publication one-step quota without raw-time accounting is insufficient if commits occur every raw Vbord; it would allow a two-pixel step each frame.
bounded_candidate_contract_review.combined_candidate: A bounded logical batch plus a raw-Vbord movement allowance is a candidate pair. A two-tick batch may admit at most one parity-selected step per actor; a minimum two-raw-Vbord publication spacing may prevent consecutive step-bearing images. The observed burst demonstrates why both dimensions matter. Neither the debt policy, guard location, global rendering effect, source fit, nor special-phase semantics is proven.
bounded_candidate_contract_review.retained_debt_effect: Reducing batch size spreads current catch-up over more foreground calls but does not remove elapsed debt. If movement opportunities are retained, they can accumulate and violate the later pixel bound; if dropped, actor travel/collision time diverges from simulation time. Any design must state whether excess movement is retained, discarded, or used to slow simulation, and prove that a missed deadline cannot create a later burst.
bounded_candidate_contract_review.special_phase_effect: The adaptive callback barriers include INITIAL_ENTRY_STATE, DEATH_STATE, PICKUP_TIMER, STAGE_PENDING, RENDER_GATE_ID, and RENDER_GATE2_ID. Any bypass list must preserve all six sources of transient/handoff work, including both gate IDs; the proposed A8FC list omitted the gates. Verify entry choreography, popup and gate frames, death timing, pickup/score order, stage transition, collision order, and movement parity.
bounded_candidate_contract_review.missed_deadline_effect: At an IRQ boundary the raw trace has up to three unfolded elapsed ticks (raw_frame - AD_LAST + stored AD_DEBT). The foreground can therefore compose multiple parity-selected movement steps before an image is published. A bound must constrain post-stall pixels while preserving contact/collision state. No repair fit or missed-deadline acceptance is established.
bounded_candidate_contract_review.bug087_interaction: BUG-087 Draft policy intentionally rises above one step per dispatch in later default Easy/Medium entries (approximately 1.2, 1.5, and 1.8; unselected hard table reaches 2.0). The candidate average of one two-pixel step per two Vbords is 1 pixel per frame: it aligns with the current Part-1 player baseline of 48 pixels/48 Vbords and historical/current enemy 1-pixel/frame baselines, but would flatten later BUG-087 speed progression if applied universally. Convert and validate the selected later-part rate policy first; preserve transient-overrun control as a separate dimension.
alternatives_and_tradeoffs: Simulation-clock cap/rebase can prevent a batch from executing multiple movement opportunities, but discarding overdue ticks slows gameplay timers, movement, AI, pickups, and other logical events against raw wall/audio time. The historical isolated fit discarded 50 overdue ticks during pickup and three during a gate continuation; those are material timing changes.
Movement-only throttling can leave actor position and collision/contact state behind the logical simulation and requires an explicit queue, discard, or slow-simulation rule.
A publication-spacing guard limits when a composed image reaches FRONT, not how many steps it contains. It can reduce burst visibility without satisfying the observed four-pixel movement bound.
Combined clock, movement, and publication guards may address distinct dimensions but require proof for debt recovery, collision ordering, owner history, special phases, and later-part rate policy.

publication_timestamp_candidate_review.status: offline candidate assessment only; no implementation, build fit, or runtime validation
candidate_sequence: Before an ordinary adaptive framebuffer_finish_back, with IRQs enabled, wait until the unsigned modulo difference between current FRAMES low byte and the stored predicted prior-publication byte at page 34:$A8FC is nonzero.

Inside framebuffer_finish_back existing IRQ-masked PENDING arm, record FRAMES+1 low byte at page 34:$A8FC and arm PENDING in the same critical section; the next Vbord IRQ is then the predicted commit.

If the previous prediction is P and the wait sees current P, continue waiting until current is P+1, then stamp next publication P+2. This spaces ordinary commits by at least two raw intervals, subject to correct first-use initialization and the pending/commit invariant.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.observed_fit: The two pixel-validated four-pixel player bursts already have two raw intervals from preceding successful commit to burst commit. A8FC minimum spacing alone would not change either measured burst; the logical batch still composed two movement steps. The timestamp guard must be paired with a separately fitted step/batch policy if the candidate movement bound is retained.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.critical_order_and_owner: Use the timestamp only in the existing IRQ-masked PENDING arm after framebuffer_capture_back and before IRQ re-enable. Stamping before capture or after IRQ re-enable can become one Vbord early if an IRQ intervenes. Prove the writer and reader execute with PAR5=34, only in the intended adaptive ownership phase, and no pending publication can cause the stamp to be overwritten prematurely.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.address_and_capacity: Parent identifies page 34:$A8FC as a candidate one-byte state location, with the current E helper ending at $A8F7 and logo candidate bytes at $A8FD-$A8FF. The proposed sequence is six code bytes plus persistent state and is not included in a verified final linked fit here. Recheck page ownership, current fitted helper capacity, source map, generated artifacts, and all hard boundaries before any prototype.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.rate1_effect: The active adaptive driver can select AD_RATE=1 after quick work. A minimum two-Vbord commit interval would then throttle every ordinary completed framebuffer image, not just moving actors: sprite poses, HUD/background changes, and other visual updates can be delayed by an extra frame. Measure effect on response and eight-tick animation dwell; the guard is not a movement-only limit.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.simulation_timers_and_audio: The wait keeps IRQs enabled, so raw FRAMES advances, but it blocks the foreground active driver before the next audio service, input, and simulation dispatch. Do not assume enabled IRQs service foreground audio. A cap/rebase paired with this wait may discard overdue simulation ticks, slowing movement, pickup/score/death and other logical timers against wall/raw time; retaining debt can preserve later catch-up and burst risk. Trace audio service and timer outcomes under the candidate.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.special_phases: The bypass must include INITIAL_ENTRY_STATE, DEATH_STATE, PICKUP_TIMER, STAGE_PENDING, RENDER_GATE_ID, and RENDER_GATE2_ID. If special frames bypass the spacing wait, still stamp each adaptive PENDING arm so the next ordinary frame is timed against the latest actual commit; initialize/rebase on the first adaptive commit.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.u8_wrap_and_initialization: FRAMES+1 low-byte wrap FF-to-00 is valid if comparison is modular. For a pure minimum-one-frame wait, test current-minus-stamp as unsigned/nonzero: an exact 256-frame alias yields zero and conservatively waits another Vbord; a signed comparison or stale/uninitialized timestamp is unsafe. Initialize/rebase the byte on first adaptive publication or ownership entry and verify reset/mode-switch paths. The spin also needs a safe recovery if raw IRQ progress stops.
publication_timestamp_candidate_review.decision: This is a pacing candidate, not a complete velocity bound or selected design. The separate cap-only comparison also misses the cumulative bound, so an A8FC guard alone or paired only with this cap cannot be claimed to meet the candidate contract. User overrun-policy choice remains pending.
